A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same crosscoder and Latent Scaling research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original crosscoder training, latent-scaling analyses, causal interventions, interpretability scores, and qualitative findings in Section 3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original Gemma experiments and additionally reports Llama replications, alternative BatchTopK experiments, and refusal-latent steering results.

M1.justification: V2 Appendix B.3 introduces two tested BatchTopK variants: selection using concatenated decoder norms and selection performed independently for each model. These change the selection procedure, although neither replaces the recommended method. The principal crosscoder architectures and closed-form Latent Scaling approach remain.

E1.justification: The versions retain FineWeb/LMSYS web-and-chat data, Ding et al. instruction prompts, LMSYS causal evaluation, and manually constructed chat examples. The Llama additions change model configurations and preprocessing; the steering example remains within the existing chat/refusal domain. No distinct dataset or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: The main L1 versus BatchTopK comparison and None, All, Error, and Template interventions remain. Appendix B.3 adds evaluated comparisons with concatenated-norm and model-independent BatchTopK variants, reporting that neither identifies more chat-specific latents than the retained approach.

E3.justification: Appendix I adds Llama 3.2 1B and 3.1 8B configurations, template-token substitutions, different sparsity settings, and 8B initialization and k-annealing procedures. Appendix N.2 adds input-only steering with specified intensities. The existing causal intervention is also reported differently: v2 Equation (4) omits the base-decoder subtraction in v1 Equation (14), although its retained All-baseline identity is inconsistent with that change. These document substantial experimental-setting additions and revisions without establishing which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds alternative-selection ablations in Appendix B.3, artifact robustness analyses on two Llama models in Appendix I, and targeted refusal-latent steering in Appendix N.2. These test architectural choices, generalization beyond Gemma, and causal interpretations of individual latents. Most earlier supplementary analyses are retained through relocation.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals for causal KL measurements and the same correlation significance thresholds. Neither specifies repeated training-run or seed counts, and v2 introduces no additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds Llama reconstruction and latent-scaling results, negative findings for the alternative BatchTopK variants, and steered refusal generations. Selected Gemma KL values also change: the BatchTopK full-response norm-ranking bars are 0.230/0.267 in v1 Figure 6a and 0.232/0.272 in v2 Figure 4a. Given the revised intervention formula, these are updated reported results rather than demonstrated same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix E.2 corrects the reconstruction targets in v1 Appendix A.5 from raw activations to reconstructed activations and fixes their beta labels. Conversely, v2 Section 2.3 incorrectly prints the reconstruction ratio as base/base instead of v1's base/chat. The revised additive intervention also no longer entails the stated All-baseline equivalence. The central decoupling argument and closed-form derivation remain.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that L1 sparsity creates misleading model-specific latents, Latent Scaling detects these artifacts, and BatchTopK identifies more genuinely chat-specific, causal, interpretable latents. The title change and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly interprets competition favoring shared latents as protection against spurious chat-only latents. Appendix N.2 interprets distinct steered refusals and eventual answers as differentiated safety mechanisms and possible self-repair. The limitations change from a single Gemma model to small models and newly question whether Latent Scaling requires crosscoders.

D1.justification: V2 replaces v1's promise of future experimental code with an explicit code location and adds training-log and demonstration-notebook access information. It newly documents initialization norms and the manual interpretation procedure. Appendix M revises the estimated reproduction budget from 60 to 180 GPU-hours and supplies hardware, stage-level costs, and larger-model cost estimates.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Betley et al. and Du et al. on fine-tuning, and explicitly connects Complete Shrinkage to SAE feature suppression, including Jermyn et al. It removes Shah et al.'s meta-token reference. The overall positioning as a refinement of crosscoder-based model diffing remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially condenses and rewrites the introduction, contributions, methods, results discussion, and limitations. It moves detailed architecture equations and the decoupling example into appendices, reorganizes results subsections, and replaces Appendix A's numbered subsections with thematic appendices A–N. These are extensive narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 changes typography and page composition, relocates the latent-classification table and coupled-latent plot, and replaces full main-text refusal displays with smaller excerpts while retaining the full display in the appendix. It adds Llama comparison figures and a steering-generation display, and relabels the independent-crosscoder plot's axes. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The Llama replications reduce v1's dependence on one model, and refusal steering adds direct evidence for interpretations previously illustrated mainly through activations. Experimental-code and log locations, initialization guidance, and compute breakdowns improve reproducibility documentation. These benefits are tempered by newly introduced reconstruction-ratio and intervention-equivalence errors, supporting a limited net improvement rather than a substantial one.
